newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies close lower on dollar shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies close lower on dollar shortcovering.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed lower as dollar short-covering turned active in the afternoon due to comments from Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse, traders and analysts said.
They said Hesse's comments that current developments in the dollar were merely part of normal fluctuations signaled that Germany would not intervene to support the mark.

June marks probed below $0.5900, as the dollar found upside momentum from model- and trend-driven fund managers who automatically covered short dollar positions once the spot rate rose above 1.7025 spot, they said.
They also said key currency contracts remained weak after U.S. retail sales and U.S. weekly jobless claims pointed to strong U.S. economic growth.
"The dollar seems to be coming back on track," one floor trader said about the dollar/mark's rise to 1.7070, which is roughly equivalent to June mark's daily low of $0.5892.
Likewise, June yen dipped to $0.008206, which corresponds near the dollar/yen's daily high of 123.45 spot.
However, losses in yen futures outstripped declines in mark futures, which found some support from mark/yen cash cross activity, traders said.
Traders said continued speculation about a possible delay in the European Monetary Union supported marks against most cash currencies, including the yen.
"It's not so much that a delay is mark-positive," one foreign exchange cash trader said. "It's more that a EMU delay would weaken other European currencies."
Still, pit traders look for a further erosion in June marks and Swiss francs on expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve will tighten rates at the March 25 Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Chicago Federal Reserve president Michael Moskow said on Thursday afternoon that the Fed must have a preemptive policy to head off inflation pressures.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was down $0.000080 at $0.008208, marks were down $0.0050 at $0.5892, Swiss francs were down $0.0066 at $0.6882, sterling fell $0.0012 to $1.5942 and Canadian dollars were down $0.0009 at $0.7372. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
